title: Binary min-heap
statement: Start simple: Build a binary min-heap with push, pop, and size. pop removes and returns the smallest value. The theory is optional. The C solution appears after the hidden tests pass.
constraints: pop on an empty heap throws IllegalStateException.
Use an array, not a library heap.
think: The smallest value stays at index 0.
Children of index i are 2i+1 and 2i+2.
Push places the value at the end and swaps it upward while it is smaller than its parent.
Pop saves the root, moves the last value there, and swaps it downward.
hints: After removing the root, shrink the size before sifting down.
Swap only while the heap property is broken.

tests.name: sorted
tests.call: { MinHeap h = new MinHeap(); h.push(3); h.push(1); h.push(2); return h.pop() + "," + h.pop() + "," + h.pop(); }

tests.name: size
tests.call: { MinHeap h = new MinHeap(); h.push(2); h.push(1); return String.valueOf(h.size()); }

tests.name: duplicates
tests.call: { MinHeap h = new MinHeap(); h.push(2); h.push(2); return h.pop() + ":" + h.size(); }

tests.name: negative
tests.call: { MinHeap h = new MinHeap(); h.push(4); h.push(-1); return String.valueOf(h.pop()); }

tests.name: many
tests.call: { MinHeap h = new MinHeap(); for (int i = 10; i >= 1; i--) h.push(i); return String.valueOf(h.pop()); }

tests.name: remaining
tests.call: { MinHeap h = new MinHeap(); h.push(5); h.push(1); h.pop(); return String.valueOf(h.pop()); }

objective: Maintain the minimum-at-root invariant while inserting and removing heap values.
workedExample: For a node at index i, its parent is (i - 1) / 2; compare upward after appending a new value.
To remove the minimum, move the last value to the root and swap it downward with its smaller child until heap order returns.
recallPrompt: Why must sift-down choose the smaller child when both children exist?

misconceptions.explanation: Choosing the left child without comparing can leave a smaller right child above the parent.
misconceptions.retry: Compare both children before choosing the next swap target.

misconceptions.explanation: Moving the last value to the root breaks order until sift-down repairs it.
misconceptions.retry: Name the two locations that can violate heap order after pop.

reflectionPrompt: Relate the array indexes in a heap to the tree shape they represent.
